title: Handoff Murmuration: Site Prep & Blockers (week of 2026-04-07)
content:
Purpose
Quick weekly snapshot capturing the standups, unusual signals, and outstanding customer blockers for active VPC/on-prem installs. This doc is the portability-focused handoff note for on-call/install teams and the solutions engineers who will be in customer-facing shifts next week. Intended to be conversational — notes to self + action log.

Attendees (floating across sessions)
- Jordan Patel (owner, lead shipper)
- Riley Chen (network specialist)
- Maya Thompson (field SRE)
- Diego Alvarez (install engineer)
- Priya Nair (solutions eng)
- CS lead: Hannah Lee (ad-hoc)

Summary (top lines)
- Two active installs: Zephyr Health (VPC peering + NFS), and Axiom Retail (on-prem, air-gapped staging).
- Zephyr: primary blocker is intermittent MTU blackholes on path between customer transit and our sidecar nodes; symptoms surface under sustained KV-cache warmups.
- Axiom: policy-managed firewall rules dropped connections to health-check ports during node reboots; root cause appears to be aggressive session timeouts in the Palo Alto rule set.
- Temporary mitigations applied for both customers; long-term fixes scheduled but need cross-team signoff (networking + security + install).

Detailed notes by customer
1) Zephyr Health (customer-facing playbook: CONFLUENCE-Page-Install-Checklist-6789)\- Observed: at ~2026-04-06T16:00 UTC, sustained inference load on a test route caused RTT spikes and occasional retransmits. Packet captures show PMTU discovery failing; traced to an intermediate transit that drops ICMP(Frag Needed).\- Impact: 5-10% of requests get stalled for ~200-800ms, appearing as token-level tail latency spikes on the console. Not a full outage, but violates our SLO for the canary route.\- Temp mitigation: enabled small-path-mtu fallback on runtime (forced 1350) and disabled jumbo frames on our sidecar NICs to reduce fragmentation. Customer agreed to lab window to trace upstream device.\- Next steps: Riley to open vendor ticket with transit provider (ticket# JIRA-INF-3421) and request explicit ICMP allow; Maya to coordinate with Zephyr network team for parallel pcap collection (done: pcap attached to JIRA).\- Risk: forcing lower MTU increases CPU for small writes; if Zephyr moves to production throughput, we need a long-term solution (either transit config change or UDP tunnel around the blackholed hop).\- Action items: Riley (due 2026-04-10) — vendor escalation; Jordan (due 2026-04-12) — schedule broad perf smoke with 50k RPS synthetic; Priya (due 2026-04-14) — propose rollback-safe config to revert forced MTU after upstream fix.

2) Axiom Retail (on-prem, staging cluster)\- Observed: repeated deploy flaps during node kernel patching; monitoring shows health-check TCP sessions reset after ~30s which causes our orchestrator to mark nodes NotReady.\- Root cause hypothesis: their firewall (Palo Alto, managed by internal NOC) has a default TCP idle timeout of 30s for the specific rule group — when kernel reboots cause orchestration to pause, the firewall tears the session and the NAT mapping fails.\- Workaround applied: introduced probe jitter and extended health-check window to 90s; added pre-drain hook to gracefully wait for KV cache flush before reboot.\- Customer ask: we need a short note they can present to their NOC explaining why connection persistence matters for our kube-managed probes. Draft provided (see linked_confluence).\- Long-term fix: coordinate with Axiom NOC to bump policy timeouts or carve a persistent rule for our management CIDR.\- Action items: Maya (due 2026-04-11) — deliver final probe-jitter change and publish patch; Diego (due 2026-04-13) — provide step-by-step remediation they can apply in their lab.

Operational signals & anomalies (week)
- Spike at 2026-04-06 16:00 UTC correlated with synthetic job 14:45 — suspicion that our synthetic didn't model head-of-line cache priming, created sustained large requests that exercised longer 90th pct.
- A few customers reported higher error rates during warmstart (prefix cache priming) when using dedicated capacity + default KV sizing. Likely common pattern: prefix sizes larger than expected cause cache thrash and longer latency.

Instrumentation notes
- Added temporary tagging for Zephyr routes: tag.install.mtu-experiment=2026-04-07. This helps filter traces for the isolation smoke next week.\- Tracing: enabled debug-level tracing only for the Zephyr canary route to limit egress. Remember to turn off after 2026-04-15.

Cross-team asks (needs attention)
- Networking: need a playbook for PMTU blackholes — short doc with commands to collect pcap, iperf tests, and vendor escalation script. Riley to draft and attach to the install playbook (Jordan to review).\- Security: Axiom needs a short form letter describing why persistent NAT sessions are required for our probes; security to approve wording. Priya to shepherd.\- Product/Runtime: consider exposing a per-install 'mtu-fallback' knob in the console so we can flip at customer-level instead of runtime-wide forced values. Product input requested by 2026-04-14.

Meeting cadence and notes (standups this week)
- Mon 2026-04-06 09:30 UTC — kick: reviewed Zephyr pcap and initial traceroutes. Action: Riley to attach vendor contacts.\- Wed 2026-04-08 15:00 UTC — deep dive: reproduced MTU symptom in lab with transit emulator; validated that forced 1350 eliminates tail spikes in synthetic.\- Thu 2026-04-09 11:00 UTC — customer sync (Zephyr): walkthrough of mitigation and plan. Customer requests visibility into rollback path.

Open decisions
- Whether to keep runtime-level forced MTU until vendor confirms fix (pros: immediate SLO improvement; cons: global perf impact for other installs). Recommendation: limit to tagged routes only (requires product change).
- Whether to propose an install-only NAT carve for Axiom. This is network + security decision; both teams asked for final signoff by 2026-04-13.

Action tracker (compact)
- INF-3421 (Riley) — escalate transit provider / collect vendor trace — due 2026-04-10.
- MTU-fallback knob (Jordan + Product) — feasibility doc — due 2026-04-14.\- Axiom probe doc (Maya) — publish patch & runbook — due 2026-04-11.

Notes to next shift
- If you see renewed tail latency on Zephyr after 04-10, fetch the pcap in the JIRA ticket and run the quick-check script (/ops/scripts/mtu_quick_check.sh).\- Do not revert forced MTU without signoff from Riley + Product; if rollback is needed immediately, flip tracing off first and run the smoke job at 5k RPS to validate.

Loose ideas / backlog (not committed)
- Build an automated PMTU probe that simulates large inference payloads before enabling production traffic (run as preflight).\- Add an install checklist item to coordinate vendor ACLs and ICMP allowances during field deployment windows.

Appendix: useful refs\- JIRA: INF-3421 (Zephyr MTU blackhole)\- Confluence: Install checklist (CONFLUENCE-Page-Install-Checklist-6789)\- Slack thread: #eng-private-install, thread id ghi123

End of note.
